input: Sync my doctor's records to a new practice

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which records are needed (full history, recent visit notes, test results, prescriptions, referrals, imaging, etc.) determines how much to request and from how many sources.
Whether this is for the user themselves, a child, or another dependent changes who must sign the release form and who manages the process.
Whether the old practice is local, in another city, or a different country affects the transfer method (in-person, mail, electronic portal) and timeline.
Some practices charge fees for record transfers; knowing if there is a cost limit shapes whether the user pursues free electronic transfer vs. paid options.
Whether both practices use compatible electronic health record (EHR) systems determines if transfer can happen digitally or must go through paper/fax.
Understanding the urgency — e.g., an upcoming appointment with the new doctor — sets the deadline and which steps to prioritise first.
The user may prefer to handle everything themselves, or may want to delegate steps to the new practice's admin team, which changes who takes the lead.

gold.taskTitle: Transfer medical records to a new practice
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to move their medical records from their current or previous doctor's practice to a new one.

questions.title: Which specific records do you need transferred?
questions.description: Identify whether the user needs their full medical history, recent visit notes, lab results, prescriptions, imaging, referral letters, or a specific subset.

questions.title: Are these records for yourself or someone else?
questions.description: Determine if the user is the patient or acting as a guardian/proxy for a child or dependent, which affects who signs the release authorisation.

questions.title: Is the old practice local, or in a different city or country?
questions.description: Understand the geographic relationship between the old and new practices to determine the most practical transfer method.

questions.title: Do both practices use an online patient portal?
questions.description: Find out if electronic health record systems are in place at either end, which determines whether transfer can be done digitally or requires paper/fax/post.

questions.title: Is there a deadline, such as an upcoming appointment?
questions.description: Establish urgency so that steps can be prioritised and a realistic timeline can be set for the transfer to be completed in time.

questions.title: Are you aware of any fees your old practice charges for this?
questions.description: Understand any cost constraints that might steer the user toward free electronic transfer options over paid printing or courier services.

questions.title: Do you want to manage this yourself or have the new practice handle it?
questions.description: Clarify the user's preferred level of involvement so the plan can either guide them step-by-step or instruct them to delegate to the new practice's admin team.
